title: Once City
era: the golden age of the cloud cities
synopsis: High over the cloud sea, Once City floats on a ring of lotus-glass domes the way the old dreamers pictured cities over Venus. Vesper Lune reopens the Lotus Lounge, the city's heart, and the whole sky comes back to dance, fall in love and fight to keep the city aloft.

world.place: A ring of lotus-shaped glass domes ribbed in gold, floating on the cloud sea over the Low Lands, held up by the turning candle towers. The Lotus Lounge is the great dome at the middle; Carat Court, the Clockwork Quarter, Pearl Passage and the Midnight Arcade lie round it on the purple walkways.
world.doors: Every district is entered through a Letter Gate, a door cut in the shape of a letter of the city's own type; read from the plaza the four main gates spell ONCE. Two lionesses, Amber and Onyx, keep the main gate, and the painted zebras, each a different colour, carry the city's post along the walkways.
people: Vesper Lune
a former Miss Cloud Sea in a pink rhinestone hat who buys back the shuttered Lotus Lounge and means to make it shine again
Pip Verdant
a green cloud sprite and the best dancer in the sky, born in the dome gardens and unable to breathe outside a dome
Jade
the jade-green lion who sleeps at the lounge's centre and wakes only for music he trusts
Amber and Onyx
the lionesses of the main Letter Gate, sisters who decide who may enter Once City
Orrin Hale
the old clockmaker who keeps the candle towers turning and the city in the air
Gideon and Greer Conroy
twin jewellers of Carat Court, rivals in business and in love
Mira Sol
the young air-pilot who flies the zebra post when the walkways fail
Silas Gray
a land baron of the Low Lands who wants Once City brought down to the ground and sold
Madame Orchid
keeper of the Midnight Arcade, who trades in secrets after twelve
Stripe
the rainbow zebra foal who refuses to carry anything but love letters

seasons.title: The Lotus Lounge
seasons.arc: Vesper reopens the Lotus Lounge, finds Pip and Jade, and learns the candle towers are failing.
episodes: The Last Lift Up
Vesper Lune rides the last working lift from the Low Lands with every coin she has and the deed to a dark dome.
Dust on the Velvet
The Lotus Lounge is full of dust and a sleeping green lion; Vesper decides to open in seven days anyway.
The Sprite in the Garden
A green sprite dances alone in the dome garden at dawn, and Vesper offers Pip Verdant a stage.
Seven Nights
Opening night: the lights fail, the band quits, and Pip dances in the dark until the whole dome claps.
The Lion Wakes
Jade the lion wakes for the first time in years to Pip's music and lies down at Vesper's feet.
Carat Court
The Conroy twins both want to dress the lounge in jewels, and each sends a gift the other must not see.
The Clockmaker
Orrin Hale tells Vesper the city sinks a finger's breadth every night the towers run slow.
Pink Chaise
A pink chaise arrives with no sender, and everyone who sits on it tells the truth.
Zebra Post
A painted zebra brings Vesper a letter from the Low Lands offering to buy her dome.
The Midnight Arcade
Pip follows a light to the Midnight Arcade and trades a dance for the name of the man who wrote the letter.
Silas Gray
The land baron Silas Gray comes up the lift in a grey coat and pays for every table in the lounge.
The Empty House
Vesper plays to a house Silas bought and left empty, and the sprites of the garden fill it instead.
Pearl Passage
The pearl divers of the cloud sea bring Vesper the first pearl of the season for luck.
Greer's Secret
Greer Conroy confesses she has been mending the lounge's chandeliers at night for free.
Tower Three
The third candle tower stops for an hour and the whole city tilts toward the clouds.
Hold the Sky
Orrin, Mira and the lift crews turn tower three by hand all night while the lounge keeps playing.
The Cowgirl Hat
Vesper's rhinestone hat goes missing on the night of the Carat ball, and the thief is a zebra foal.
Stripe
Stripe the rainbow foal will carry only love letters, which makes him the busiest zebra in Once City.
Gideon's Ring
Gideon makes a ring for someone he will not name and leaves it in the lounge's lost and found.
Dance of the Domes
Pip teaches the whole Pearl Passage a dance and the walkways shake with it.
Air Pilot
Mira Sol flies the post through a storm when the walkways are closed and lands on the lounge roof.
The Velvet Rope
Vesper turns away a duchess for being rude to the staff and the duchess starts a rival lounge.
The Rival Lounge
The Silver Bell opens across the plaza with stolen dancers and twice the lights.
Green Light
Pip is offered a fortune to dance at the Silver Bell and walks over the plaza to say no in person.
The Lionesses
Amber and Onyx refuse Silas Gray entry at the main gate, and the whole city hears about it.
The Letter Gate
Orrin shows Vesper that the main gate is a letter, and that one letter of the city's name is missing.
Night of Lanterns
The Pearl Passage floats its lanterns and every one drifts toward the Lotus Lounge.
The Ledger
Vesper finds the old lounge ledger and learns her mother once danced on the same stage.
Down a Breadth
The city sinks a full breadth in one night and the cloud sea touches the lowest walkway.
The Bid
Silas offers to save the towers if the city lets him own them; the council votes in the lounge.
One Vote
The vote is tied, and the last vote belongs to whoever owns the Lotus Lounge.
Vesper Votes
Vesper votes no, Jade roars for the first time in a century, and the towers start to turn faster.

seasons.title: The Letter Gates
seasons.arc: The city's gates are letters of its own type; the missing letter is found and the lionesses and the zebras keep the city whole.
episodes: The Fifth Gate
Orrin's maps show a fifth Letter Gate no one has opened, sealed under the Midnight Arcade.
Amber Speaks
Amber the lioness lets Vesper through the main gate at night and leads her round the walls.
Onyx Waits
Onyx stays at the gate alone and stops a crate of Silas's tools from coming in.
The Zebra Stables
Vesper visits the painted zebras' stables and learns each colour carries a different kind of news.
Blue Is Bad News
A blue zebra trots into the lounge and nobody wants to open the letter on its saddle.
The Missing O
The letter missing from ONCE is the O, the round gate that was taken down in the old war.
Pip's Fever
Pip falls ill when the dome garden's air runs thin and the whole lounge holds its breath.
Garden Air
Greer and Gideon trade their best pearls for the glass to mend the garden dome.
The Duchess Returns
The rival duchess of the Silver Bell needs Vesper's help when her dome cracks.
Two Lounges, One Night
The Silver Bell and the Lotus Lounge put on one show together and the plaza overflows.
Stripe in Love
Stripe the rainbow foal carries a letter that is for him, from a grey mare in the Low Lands.
Down the Lift
Mira flies Stripe down to the Low Lands to meet the grey mare, and they find Silas's workshops.
The Workshops
Below the clouds Silas is building iron towers that would pull the city down onto his land.
The Mare
The grey mare is Silas's own, and she wants to go up to the city with Stripe.
Coming Home
Stripe and the grey mare ride the lift up and Onyx lets them both through the gate.
Madame Orchid's Price
Madame Orchid will open the arcade's sealed gate if Vesper sings one secret on stage.
The Secret Song
Vesper sings that she once sold the lounge's lease to Silas when she was young and broke.
After the Song
The lounge forgives her, Pip does not speak to her for a day, and Jade sleeps at her door.
Under the Arcade
Behind the sealed gate is a great round door of gold, the lost O of Once City.
Too Heavy
The O is too heavy to lift; every walkway would crack if it were moved by hand.
The Zebra Train
Every painted zebra in the city pulls together, colour by colour, to bring the O to the plaza.
Pearl and Gold
Greer and Gideon set pearls into the O and finally say what the ring in the lost and found was for.
Raising the Gate
The city raises the O at the plaza and, for the first time, the gates spell ONCE.
The Gate Remembers
When the O stands, the candle towers turn by themselves and the city rises a breadth.
Silas's Iron
Silas switches on his iron towers below and the city shudders against the pull.
The Tug
Every night the city and the iron towers pull against each other while the lounge plays louder.
Lionesses on the Wall
Amber and Onyx walk the walls every night, roaring whenever the iron pulls.
The Clockmaker's Son
Orrin admits his son works for Silas and built the iron towers.
Hale and Son
Orrin goes down the lift to talk to his son, and only Mira knows he went.
The Son Comes Up
Tobin Hale comes up to Once City to see what his father kept turning all his life.
Tobin Dances
Tobin sees Pip dance and switches off one of the iron towers from the lounge's stage.
Half the Iron
Half the iron goes dark, the city settles, and Silas swears he will come up himself.

seasons.title: Storm Season
seasons.arc: Silas comes up in the storm season; the lounge, the gates and the people of the domes hold the city together.
episodes: The Storm Bell
The storm bell rings over the cloud sea, the season when nothing comes up the lift.
Locked In
No one can leave the city for a month, and the Lotus Lounge becomes everyone's home.
Thirty Nights
Vesper promises a different show for every storm night and runs out of ideas by the fourth.
Everyone Sings
The lounge lets the guests take the stage, and a shy watchmaker steals the season.
Lightning in the Glass
Lightning cracks the Clockwork Quarter's dome and the clocks stop at a quarter past nine.
Quarter Past Nine
With every clock stopped, the city lives one long evening that nobody wants to end.
Silas in the Storm
Silas Gray comes up in an airship through the storm and lands on the plaza in the rain.
Guest of the Lounge
Vesper gives Silas a table, because the Lotus Lounge has never turned anyone away in a storm.
The Land Baron Dances
Pip asks Silas to dance, and he does, badly, and laughs for the first time in the story.
What Silas Wants
Silas tells Vesper the city's weight is ruining his land and the people below can't grow anything.
The Shadow Below
Mira flies under the city and sees the dark the floating city casts on the Low Lands.
A Fair Question
The council must decide whether a city in the sky owes anything to the land it shades.
Greer's Plan
Greer suggests mirrors under the domes to send light down to the farms below.
Mirror Work
The whole city works through the storm to hang mirrors under the walkways.
Pip Can't Go
Pip wants to help below but can't breathe outside a dome, and Jade will not leave her side.
The Glass Bubble
Tobin builds Pip a glass helmet so she can dance outside the domes for one hour.
One Hour Outside
Pip dances on the outer walkway in the storm for one hour and the zebras dance with her.
Madame Orchid's Book
Madame Orchid lends Vesper a book of every bargain ever made in Once City.
The First Bargain
The book shows the city's founders promised the Low Lands light and forgot.
Founders' Debt
Vesper reads the founders' promise aloud in the lounge, and the room goes quiet.
Stripe's Foal
Stripe and the grey mare have a foal with grey and rainbow stripes.
Lionesses' Cubs
Amber has three cubs in the gatehouse and Onyx keeps the gate alone again.
Light Below
The first mirror light reaches the Low Lands' fields, and the farmers wave up at the city.
Silas Watches
Silas stands at the edge of the plaza and watches the light fall on his own land.
The Iron Goes Dark
Silas switches off the last iron tower himself.
The Clocks Start
The storm breaks, the Clockwork Quarter's clocks start again, and the long evening ends.
After the Storm
The lift runs again and half the Low Lands comes up to see the lounge.
The Duchess Proposes
The duchess of the Silver Bell proposes the two lounges become one.
Two Names
Vesper and the duchess argue over the name for a whole episode and settle on keeping both.
Gideon Leaves
Gideon goes down to the Low Lands to set up a jeweller's school, and Greer stays.
The Ring Returns
Greer finds the ring from the lost and found on her pillow with a zebra-post note.
Storm's End Ball
The storm's end ball fills every dome, and Silas Gray buys a ticket like everyone else.

seasons.title: Once and Always
seasons.arc: Once City chooses what it will be: it rises, it shares its light, and the Lotus Lounge passes to the next dancers.
episodes: The Last Pageant
Once City holds the first Miss Cloud Sea pageant since Vesper won it, and she is asked to judge.
Contestants
Twelve contestants from twelve domes arrive, and one of them is Mira the air-pilot.
Pip's Pupil
Pip takes on a pupil, a girl from the Low Lands who has never seen a dome.
The Rise
Orrin says the towers could lift the city into the high air where storms can't reach.
Higher or Here
The city debates rising out of reach or staying close to the land it now lights.
Tobin's Machine
Tobin builds a lift that can reach the city from anywhere below, not just one tower.
Many Lifts
Lifts go down to every village in the Low Lands, and the city fills with new faces.
Crowded Domes
The domes are full, rents rise, and Vesper fights to keep the lounge open to everyone.
Free Night
The Lotus Lounge declares one free night a week, and the queue reaches the gates.
Amber's Cubs Grow
Amber's cubs learn to guard the gate and let in only people who smile at them.
Painted Zebras
The painted zebras win the vote to become the city's official post, colour by colour.
Madame Orchid's Last Secret
Madame Orchid closes the Midnight Arcade and tells Vesper who sent the pink chaise.
The Chaise
The pink chaise was sent by Vesper's mother before she died, for the day the lounge reopened.
Mother's Stage
Vesper dances, for the first time in the story, on the stage her mother danced on.
Jade Grows Old
Jade the lion sleeps longer every day, and Pip plays only the songs he trusts.
The Green Sleep
Jade falls asleep for good during the softest song, and the whole city dims its lights.
After Jade
The lounge is quiet for a week, until Stripe's foal walks in and lies where Jade lay.
The Final Round
The pageant's final round is a dance, and Mira wins it flying her airship to the music.
Mira's Crown
Mira wears the crown for one night and gives it to Pip's pupil from the Low Lands.
Greer and Gideon
Gideon comes back up the lift with his first class of jewellers, and Greer is at the gate.
A Wedding in Carat Court
Greer and Gideon marry under the O gate, and the zebras carry every invitation.
Silas's Toast
Silas Gray gives a toast at the wedding and admits Once City was worth more in the air.
The Vote Again
The council votes once more: rise high, or stay low and share the light.
Stay
The city votes to stay, and Orrin locks the towers at the height where the mirrors reach every field.
Orrin's Rest
Orrin hands the towers to Tobin and sits down for the first time in forty years.
The Lounge Passes
Vesper decides it is time to give the Lotus Lounge to the next keeper.
Who Keeps It
Pip, the duchess and Mira each think they should have it, and none of them asks for it.
Pip's Answer
Pip says the lounge should belong to whoever dances on its stage that night.
Everyone Dances
On the last night everyone in the city dances on the stage, so the lounge belongs to all of them.
The Letter Gates Open
Every Letter Gate stands open at once, and the lionesses lie down in the sun.
Vesper's Hat
Vesper leaves her rhinestone hat on the pink chaise for the next queen of the cloud sea.
Once
The lights go down over the domes, the cloud sea turns gold, and Once City is still there in the morning.
